words.gloss: of whatever nature it may be

literal: Whatever thing, of whatever nature it may be, that thing's true essence to discern is wisdom.
translation: To discern the true essence of any thing, whatever its apparent nature may be, is wisdom.
modern: எந்த ஒரு பொருளும் எத்தகைய தன்மையைக் கொண்டதாக இருந்தாலும், அப்பொருளின் உண்மையான இயல்பைக் காண்பதே அறிவாகும்.
explanation: This couplet defines true wisdom as the ability to look beyond superficial appearances to find the ultimate truth. Things in the world present themselves in various forms and natures, which can often be deceptive or temporary. True knowledge does not stop at these outward characteristics but penetrates to the core reality of the object. The word 'meypporuḷ' (true essence) contrasts with 'ettanmaittu' (whatever nature), emphasizing the difference between transient qualities and permanent truth.
